To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) certain HIV‐1 infected individuals develop a specific host response, termed DILS, characterized by tissue‐infiltrating CD8 T‐lymphocytes and monocyte‐tropism of HIV‐1, and (2) this host response is genetically controlled by MHC class II and class I genes, in a dominant manner.

1) DILS is an autoimmune‐like disorder in HIV‐1 infection that involves a specific host‐response to HIV‐1; 2) this host‐response leads to persistence of HIV‐1 strains that infect monocytes and other cells of the monocyte‐macrophage lineage; and, 3) this host‐ response is regulated by both maternal and paternal MHC class II gene products in a dominant fashion.
DILS is a host‐response disease caused by HIV‐1, that is characterized by circulating and target tissue CD8 T lymphocytosis.
